strengths: UniAP addresses a useful training-infrastructure problem by jointly selecting pipeline placement and DP, TP, and FSDP strategies. Accounting for memory limits, resharding, and inter-stage communication is relevant to training large vision models.

Table 2 demonstrates meaningful practical gains. On EnvB, ViT throughput increases from the strongest baseline's 38.74 to 45.58 samples/s, and Swin improves from 13.90 to 19.08 samples/s. UniAP also successfully runs Swin on EnvA where Galvatron encounters OOM. These results establish value across multiple architectures and interconnect configurations.

Reported planning times are substantially shorter in several settings: BERT on EnvA takes 0.37 minutes versus Galvatron's 6.44 minutes. The cost-model evaluation, topology-aware case study, algorithm pseudocode, and detailed model and solver configurations provide useful supporting evidence and improve clarity.
weaknesses: The central formulation has a consequential correctness gap. Equations (6a–c) enforce contiguity within each stage, but do not enforce topological ordering between stages. For a two-layer graph u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies these constraints, yet Equation (4) assigns zero communication cost because it counts only edges from stage j to j+1. The objective can therefore favor an assignment with omitted communication. Edges spanning nonconsecutive stages are also unaccounted for. Appendix A proves contiguity, which does not resolve this problem.

The presented optimization is not an MIQP as written. Equations (3–4) contain fourth-degree products of decision variables, such as P_ui P_vi S_uk S_vl. These products can be reformulated using auxiliary variables, but the manuscript supplies neither that reformulation nor its linking constraints and resulting problem size. This is a substantial reproducibility gap because the solver formulation is the principal methodological contribution.

Claims of optimality and computational complexity exceed the evidence. Appendix D specifies a 60-second time limit and permits stopping after 15 seconds with an optimality gap below 4%; achieved gaps and timeout frequencies are unreported. Algorithm 1 also restricts pipeline degrees and micro-batch counts. Consequently, global optimality is not established. Section 3.5's complexity argument treats solver time as constant and omits explicit dependence on micro-batch enumeration and pairwise strategy costs; a runtime cap does not establish the complexity of finding an optimum.

The experiments do not isolate the claimed advantage of joint optimization over hierarchical optimization. Figure 7 removes entire categories of parallelism, establishing the usefulness of hybrid strategies rather than the superiority of the proposed search procedure. Comparisons additionally differ in cost-model accuracy and, for Alpa, execution framework. Hierarchical optimization is not inherently suboptimal, and no matched comparison or exhaustive small-instance validation establishes the claimed distinction. Figure 6 evaluates selected strategies only, so its low estimation error does not establish correct ranking across the search space.

The efficiency comparison has incomplete accounting: UniAP's reported optimization time measures UOP and excludes preceding profiling, while equivalent timing boundaries and CPU-thread budgets for the baselines are not established. The scalability experiment also increases batch size alongside device count, supporting a limited weak-scaling result. These limitations constrain the efficiency claims; together with the central formulation and validation gaps, they outweigh the otherwise worthwhile measured improvements and determine the weak-reject recommendation.
